18044:
Recall the diagnostic chordate characters and the fate of the notochord
The central nervous system is dorsal, hollow and single, and in vertebrates the embryonic notochord is replaced by the vertebral column
In urochordates the notochord is present only in the larval tail, and Hemichordata is no longer placed under Chordata
Hence b and c true with a and d false, which is option C
→ (C)
18045:
Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus spills glucose into urine (glycosuria) because blood glucose exceeds the renal threshold for reabsorption
Fat breakdown in insulin deficiency releases ketone bodies that also appear in urine (ketonuria)
Uremia means excess urea in blood from kidney failure and renal calculi are kidney stones, neither specific to diabetes
Hence glycosuria with ketonuria marks diabetes, which is option B
→ (B)
18046:
Translation begins with activation of amino acids, called aminoacylation or charging of tRNA
Each amino acid is linked to its specific tRNA by aminoacyl tRNA synthetase using ATP energy
Only after charging does mRNA bind the ribosome and codon-anticodon recognition proceed
Hence the first step is aminoacylation, which is option B
→ (B)
18047:
Ray florets belong to the capitulum inflorescence of the Asteraceae family with an epigynous flower
In epigyny the thalamus grows around the ovary so the floral parts arise above it
Such an ovary position is termed inferior, as also seen in disc florets, which is option D
→ (D)
18048:
Growth is slowest in the lag phase when cells acclimatise, and fastest once division becomes exponential
This exponential stage of the growth curve is the log phase with maximum increase in size or number
Senescence and dormancy show declining or arrested growth, not the peak, so the log phase is option D
→ (D)
18049:
Fibrous roots form a cluster arising from the base of the stem, typical of monocots such as wheat
The primary root develops from the radicle, prop roots grow from stem nodes for support, and lateral roots branch from the primary root
Only the base-of-stem origin matches the description given, which is option D
→ (D)
18050:
True hydrophily uses water as the pollinating agent, as in Vallisneria and Zostera
Water hyacinth and water lily rise above the surface and are pollinated by insects or wind instead
Hence they are entomophilous or anemophilous despite their aquatic habitat, which is option D
→ (D)
18051:
Secondary treatment produces activated sludge, a mass of aerobic flocs that settles in the tank
A part is recycled as inoculum while the remainder is pumped into the anaerobic sludge digester
There anaerobic bacteria digest the sludge to biogas, unlike primary sludge or screened debris, so the effluent sludge is option C
→ (C)
18052:
Acoelomate triploblasts lack any body cavity between gut and body wall
Platyhelminthes such as Planaria combine this plan with bilateral symmetry
Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomate, annelids are coelomate, and ctenophores are radially symmetrical
Hence Planaria is the answer, which is option A
→ (A)
18053:
Basic amino acids carry an extra amino group in the side chain, giving lysine, arginine and histidine
Glutamic acid is acidic with an extra carboxyl group, while valine and tyrosine are neutral
Lysine is therefore the only basic amino acid among the options, which is option B
→ (B)
18054:
Embryo transfer methods place cultured embryos into the mother to assist conception
ZIFT transfers the zygote or early embryo up to eight blastomeres into the fallopian tube
IUT transfers embryos with more than eight blastomeres into the uterus
Hence the pair is ZIFT and IUT, which is option D
→ (D)
18055:
Inclusion bodies are cytoplasmic storage granules of phosphate, glycogen or lipid held in reserve
They lie free in the cytoplasm and are not enclosed by any membrane
Ingestion of food particles is carried out by phagosomes
Hence the phagosome statement about inclusion bodies is incorrect, which is option A
→ (A)
18056:
Sutton and Boveri proposed the chromosomal theory linking Mendelian factors to chromosomes
Its experimental proof came from Morgan Drosophila crosses showing sex-linked inheritance and linkage
Mendel formulated the laws of inheritance but worked without any knowledge of chromosomes
Hence Morgan provided the experimental verification, which is option C
→ (C)
18057:
Gonorrhoea, syphilis and genital herpes all spread through sexual contact
Malaria and filaria are vector-borne diseases transmitted by mosquitoes, and cancer is non-communicable
Only the gonorrhoea-syphilis-genital herpes set contains exclusively sexually transmitted diseases, which is option D
→ (D)
18058:
Human insulin is synthesised as proinsulin with an extra C-peptide joining the A and B chains
Maturation removes the C-peptide and the two chains stay joined by disulphide bridges
Linkage by hydrogen bonds is therefore wrong, and engineered insulin is produced in E. coli
Hence the hydrogen-bond statement is incorrect, which is option B
→ (B)
18059:
Golgi bodies modify proteins received from the endoplasmic reticulum by glycosylation
Addition of carbohydrate chains there forms glycoproteins and glycolipids for secretion or membranes
Polysomes only translate proteins and peroxisomes handle oxidation, not glycosylation
Hence glycosylation in the Golgi is the answer, which is option B
→ (B)
18060:
Recall the standard industrial microbe-product pairs
Clostridium butylicum ferments sugars to butyric acid and Trichoderma polysporum yields the immunosuppressant Cyclosporin-A
Monascus purpureus gives statins that lower blood cholesterol and Aspergillus niger is the commercial source of citric acid
The correct match is therefore (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii), which is option A
→ (A)
18061:
Embryological support for evolution rested on the recapitulation claim that embryos replay ancestral adult stages
Karl Ernst von Baer rejected this through his laws showing that general characters appear before special characters in development
Darwin and Wallace proposed natural selection and Oparin worked on the origin of life
Hence the scientist who disapproved the embryological argument is Karl Ernst von Baer, which is option D
→ (D)
18062:
The origin of replication, called the Ori site, is the sequence from which replication starts and which sets the copy number of the linked DNA in a vector
Palindromic sequences act as recognition sites for restriction enzymes and selectable markers only permit identification of transformants
Since copy number control is the defining role of the origin, the required sequence is the Ori site, which is option A
→ (A)
18063:
Viroids are the smallest known infectious agents, consisting of free low molecular weight RNA without any protein coat
They replicate inside plant cells and cause diseases such as potato spindle tuber disease
DNA with a coat describes viruses, so the correct description of viroids is free RNA without a protein coat, which is option A
→ (A)
18064:
The Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987 to phase out chlorofluorocarbons and other substances that deplete stratospheric ozone
Control of greenhouse gases came through later climate agreements while e-waste disposal and transboundary movement of modified organisms fall under separate conventions
The 1987 protocol therefore concerns emission of ozone depleting substances, which is option A
→ (A)
18065:
In each turn of the citric acid cycle only the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate is coupled to direct GTP formation by succinyl-CoA synthetase
All other ATP equivalents of the cycle arise indirectly through NADH and FADH_{2} oxidation in the electron transport chain
One turn of the cycle therefore involves a single substrate level phosphorylation, which is option A
→ (A)
18066:
During the late follicular phase rising estrogen from the maturing Graafian follicle switches to positive feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary
This triggers the mid-cycle LH surge which ruptures the follicle and releases the ovum
High progesterone instead maintains pregnancy while low LH or low FSH cannot cause rupture
Hence ovulation is induced by a high concentration of estrogen, which is option D
→ (D)
18067:
Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a point mutation in the beta-globin gene on chromosome 11 and is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait
Phenylketonuria and thalassemia are also autosomal recessive rather than dominant or X linked, and haemophilia is X linked recessive rather than Y linked
The only fully correct pairing is therefore sickle cell anaemia with autosomal recessive inheritance on chromosome 11, which is option B
→ (B)
18068:
Cuboidal epithelium bearing a dense brush border of microvilli is specialised for absorption and lines the proximal convoluted tubule of the nephron
Ducts of salivary glands carry cuboidal cells without a brush border and the Eustachian tube is lined by ciliated epithelium
The lining of the intestine is columnar with microvilli rather than cuboidal
Hence the described tissue belongs to the proximal convoluted tubule, which is option B
→ (B)
18069:
Over Antarctica the thinned ozone layer lets high doses of UV-B radiation reach the surface, where reflection from snow further increases exposure
UV-B inflames the cornea, a painful photokeratitis commonly called snow-blindness
Infra-red retinal damage, simple glare, or freezing of eye fluids do not describe this pathology
Hence the cause is corneal inflammation by UV-B radiation, which is option A
→ (A)
18070:
Chlorella is a unicellular green alga and Spirulina is a unicellular cyanobacterium harvested as single-celled protein
Gelidium and Gracilaria are multicellular red algae while Laminaria and Sargassum are large multicellular brown algae
Anabaena is filamentous and Volvox is a colonial coenobium
Hence the unicellular algal pair is Chlorella and Spirulina, which is option C
→ (C)
18071:
Scattered vascular bundles in a conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue with each bundle conjoint, closed and sheathed is the anatomy of a monocotyledonous stem
Roots carry radial vascular bundles while dicotyledonous stems show bundles in a ring with open collateral organisation and phloem parenchyma present
Absence of phloem parenchyma further confirms the monocot pattern
Hence the section is a monocotyledonous stem, which is option D
→ (D)
18072:
Mendel worked with seven pairs of contrasting characters in pea, selecting true breeding lines that differed in only one character at a time
Seven characters with two contrasting traits each gives fourteen distinct true breeding varieties
Counts of two, four or eight varieties would cover only some of the experimental pairs
Hence the number selected is fourteen, which is option B
→ (B)
18073:
Floridean starch is the stored glucan of red algae with alpha-1,4 linked chains and alpha-1,6 branch points
This branched architecture matches amylopectin and glycogen rather than linear cellulose or laminarin
Mannitol and algin are brown algal products with unrelated chemistry
Hence Floridean starch resembles amylopectin and glycogen, which is option A
→ (A)
18074:
In the G_{1} phase the cell is metabolically active, grows in size and synthesises proteins and organelles without replicating its DNA
DNA synthesis is confined to the S phase and nuclear division occurs in the M phase
Reorganisation of cell components for division characterises the G_{2} phase
Hence the correct statement for G_{1} is a growing cell with no DNA replication, which is option B
→ (B)
18075:
Cross breeding mates a superior male of one breed with a superior female of another breed so that desirable characters of both breeds combine in the progeny
Hisardale sheep was produced by crossing Bikaneri ewes with Marino rams, two distinct breeds
Inbreeding and outcrossing occur within the same breed
Hence Hisardale is a cross breed, which is option B
→ (B)
18076:
Active immunity develops when the host itself produces antibodies after exposure to antigen, so it is slow to build up
Passive immunity from ready-made antibodies acts immediately
Foetal antibodies received from the mother and directly injected antisera are both passive
Hence the claim that active immunity is quick with full response is incorrect, which is option B
→ (B)
18077:
EcoRI scans DNA for a specific palindromic hexanucleotide and cuts between G and A to leave sticky overhangs
The recognised sequence reads 5-GAATTC-3 on one strand and 3-CTTAAG-5 on the complementary strand
BamHI recognises GGATCC instead
Hence the EcoRI sequence is GAATTC, which is option D
→ (D)
18078:
Length of double-helical DNA equals the number of base pairs multiplied by the rise per base pair of 0.34 nm
Multiplying 6.6 \times 10^{9} bp by 0.34 nm gives about 2.244 \times 10^{9} nm
This converts to roughly 2.24 m, approximately 2.2 meters, which is option B
→ (B)
18079:
The cockroach nervous system is spread along the ventral body with segmental ganglia that locally control most reflexes and movements
The head holds only a small anterior portion with the brain
A headless body retains ventral cord function and survives for some days, which is option B
→ (B)
18080:
In a grassland the first trophic level holds producers, the second holds primary consumers, the third holds secondary consumers and the fourth holds top consumers
Grass is the producer, rabbit the herbivore, crow the secondary consumer and vulture the top consumer
The code a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i is option D
→ (D)
18081:
Pancreatic trypsin is secreted as inactive trypsinogen to prevent self-digestion and is activated in the small intestine
Enterokinase secreted by the intestinal mucosa cleaves trypsinogen into active trypsin
Trypsin then activates the other pancreatic proenzymes
Hence enterokinase activates trypsinogen, which is option A
→ (A)
18082:
The ileum is the long highly coiled terminal part of the small intestine adapted for absorption
Serosa is the outermost covering of the gut wall
Vermiform appendix arises from the caecum and the ileum opens into the large intestine
Hence only the coiled ileum statement is correct, which is option B
→ (B)
18083:
Gibberellins promote internode elongation by stimulating both cell division and cell elongation in stem tissue
Spraying sugarcane with gibberellin lengthens the stem and raises cane and sugar yield
Ethylene, abscisic acid and cytokinin do not give this response
Hence gibberellin is the answer, which is option A
→ (A)
18084:
Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific palindromic sites and are key tools of genetic engineering
Each enzyme inspects a defined sequence length
Complementary sticky overhangs join by base pairing while ligase merely seals the phosphodiester nicks
Hence the ligase-joins-sticky-ends statement is the intended wrong one, which is option C
→ (C)
18085:
Malonate competitively inhibits catalytic activity, collagen is a protein carrying peptide bonds, chitin forms the fungal cell wall and ricin is a plant secondary metabolite
This gives (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(i), which is option D
→ (D)
18086:
Goblet cells are unicellular mucus-secreting glands scattered in the gut epithelium that lubricate and protect the mucosal surface
They arise as modified columnar epithelial cells rather than from squamous, compound epithelial cells or chondrocytes
Hence goblet cells arise from columnar epithelium, which is option A
→ (A)
18087:
Cyclostomes carry 6-15 pairs of gill slits, cartilaginous fishes carry a heterocercal caudal fin, bony fishes carry an air bladder and Trygon carries a poison sting
This gives (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i), which is option D
→ (D)
18088:
The synaptonemal complex holds homologous chromosomes together during zygotene pairing and pachytene crossing over
It dissolves at diplotene so homologues separate except at chiasmata, well after leptotene condensation
Hence it dissolves at diplotene, which is option B
→ (B)
18089:
During transcription the DNA duplex around the promoter must locally unwind so the template strand becomes accessible
RNA polymerase itself melts and opens the helix to initiate RNA synthesis
DNA helicase of replication, DNA polymerase and DNA ligase do not perform this opening
Hence RNA polymerase opens the helix, which is option C
→ (C)
18090:
In DNA adenine on one strand pairs with thymine on the opposite strand through two hydrogen bonds
Guanine pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds
Options claiming one bond, three bonds or no pairing for A-T therefore contradict complementary base pairing
Only the two hydrogen bond description of the A-T pair is correct, which is option D
→ (D)
18091:
Species diversity increases from high latitudes toward the equator, so tropical rain forests hold the richest biota
Among the listed regions the Amazon rain forest carries the largest number of plant, bird, mammal and insect species
Madagascar, the Himalayas and the Western Ghats are rich hotspots but hold fewer species
Hence the Amazon holds maximum diversity, which is option C
→ (C)
18092:
Deficiency of ADH from the pituitary causes diabetes insipidus, so pituitary matches diabetes insipidus
Hyperthyroidism in Grave disease links the thyroid, Addison disease links underactive adrenal cortex, and insulin deficiency links the pancreas with diabetes mellitus
That gives pituitary-iii, thyroid-i, adrenal-iv and pancreas-ii, which is option B
→ (B)
18093:
Nitrogenase in legume root nodules reduces atmospheric dinitrogen under anaerobic conditions using ATP and reducing power
The reaction is N_{2} + 8H^{+} + 8e^{-} + 16ATP \rightarrow 2NH_{3} + H_{2} + 16ADP + 16P_{i}
Ammonia and hydrogen are therefore the products, and nitrate or oxygen are not formed, which is option C
→ (C)
18094:
Iron is required for chlorophyll biosynthesis and ferredoxin, while zinc is needed for auxin (IAA) biosynthesis
Boron supports pollen germination and sugar transport, and manganese drives photolysis of water in photosystem II
That gives iron-iii, zinc-iv, boron-ii and manganese-i, which is option B
→ (B)
18095:
Aldosterone from the adrenal cortex acts on distal tubules and collecting ducts to increase reabsorption of \text{Na}^{+} and water
Greater water reabsorption concentrates urine and reduces its volume, opposing diuresis
ANF promotes sodium loss, low renin lowers aldosterone and low ADH reduces water reabsorption
Hence aldosterone causes diuresis prevention, which is option A
→ (A)
18096:
The secondary oocyte arrests in metaphase II after meiosis I and is released at ovulation
Meiosis II resumes only when a sperm contacts and fuses with the ovum during fertilisation
Completion at copulation, after zygote formation or before ovulation is incorrect
Hence fusion with the ovum completes meiosis II, which is option C
→ (C)
18097:
Locusta is the gregarious polyphagous locust pest, and Asterias shows radial adults with bilateral larvae as an echinoderm
Scorpions respire through book lungs, while Ctenoplana shows bioluminescence among ctenophores
That gives a-iv, b-i, c-ii and d-iii, which is option A
→ (A)
18098:
Floating ribs are the eleventh and twelfth pairs that do not connect with the sternum
Acromion is the flat process of the clavicle region of the pectoral girdle
The scapula lies dorsally between the second and seventh ribs, and the glenoid cavity articulates with the head of the humerus
That gives a-iv, b-iii, c-i and d-ii, which is option C
→ (C)
18099:
Primary metabolites such as sugars and amino acids directly support growth and reproduction
Nicotine, strychnine and caffeine are alkaloid secondary metabolites that deter herbivores and pathogens
They therefore serve a protective defence role rather than nutrition or growth, which is option B
→ (B)
18100:
Bt cotton carries cry genes from Bacillus thuringiensis, and ADA deficiency was the first case treated by gene therapy
RNAi silences genes as a cellular defence mechanism, while PCR amplifies nucleic acids for early detection of HIV infection
That gives a-iv, b-i, c-ii and d-iii, which is option D
→ (D)
18101:
Miller recreated the reducing primitive atmosphere with methane, hydrogen, ammonia and water vapour in a closed flask
Electric discharge supplied energy with the mixture held near 800\degree C, forming amino acids within days
Any mixture with CH_{3} or with 600\degree C misstates the experiment, which is option D
→ (D)
18102:
Bacillus thuringiensis yields insecticidal Cry proteins, and Thermus aquaticus yields heat-stable Taq DNA polymerase used in PCR
Agrobacterium tumefaciens provides the Ti plasmid cloning vector, while the first rDNA molecule was built in Salmonella typhimurium
That gives a-iv, b-iii, c-i and d-ii, which is option A
→ (A)
18103:
The introduced cry toxin gene expresses Cry protein that forms pores in the insect midgut after ingestion
The protein targets bollworm and related insect pests rather than fungi or nematodes
Field resistance is therefore against insect pests, which is option D
→ (D)
18104:
DNA ligase seals nicks and joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds between molecules
Polymerases synthesise new strands, nucleases cleave phosphodiester bonds, and exonucleases remove nucleotides from free ends rather than cutting internally
Only the ligase pairing is stated correctly, which is option D
→ (D)
18105:
The funicle is the stalk that joins the ovule to the placenta and supplies it
The region where the body of the ovule fuses with the funicle forms a scar called the hilum
Micropyle is the small opening at the tip, chalaza is the basal end and nucellus is the central nutritive tissue
Hence the funicle-placenta junction scar is the hilum, which is option D
→ (D)
18106:
A strobilus is a compact cone-like aggregation of sporophylls bearing sporangia
Among pteridophytes Equisetum bears distinct terminal strobili on fertile axes
Pteris and Salvinia are ferns without cones and Marchantia is a liverwort with gemmae and archegoniophores
Hence Equisetum bears strobili, which is option C
→ (C)
18107:
Eosinophils release histaminase and destructive enzymes against parasites, giving (a) to (iii)
Basophils release granules loaded with histamine and heparin, giving (b) to (iv)
Neutrophils are phagocytic while lymphocytes mediate humoral and cell mediated immune response
Hence (c) to (ii) and (d) to (i), which is option D
→ (D)
18108:
Glycosidic bonds join monosaccharide units in carbohydrates while peptide bonds join amino acids in proteins
Inulin is a fructose polymer with glycosidic bonds and insulin is a protein hormone with peptide bonds
Glycerol, lecithin, cholesterol are lipids without these bonds and chitin paired with cholesterol fails the peptide part
Hence inulin with glycosidic and insulin with peptide bonds is option C
→ (C)
18109:
Gross primary productivity is the total rate of organic matter produced in photosynthesis
Plants use a large part of it in respiration and the remainder is net primary productivity
Hence NPP equals GPP minus respiratory loss, so GPP is always greater than NPP, which is option A
→ (A)
18110:
Placenta secretes human chorionic gonadotropin, giving (a) to (ii)
Zona pellucida is the glycoprotein layer around the ovum, giving (b) to (iii)
Bulbo-urethral glands lubricate the penis while Leydig cells of the testis secrete androgens
Hence (c) to (iv) and (d) to (i), which is option C
→ (C)
18111:
Population attributes describe features of members of one species in an area such as natality, mortality, sex ratio, age distribution and density
Species interaction describes association between members of different species such as predation, competition and mutualism
It is therefore a property of a community, not of a single population, which is option C
→ (C)
18112:
Organ of Corti with sensory hair cells rests on the basilar membrane, giving (a) to (iv)
Cochlea is the coiled part of the inner ear labyrinth, giving (b) to (ii)
Eustachian tube connects middle ear with pharynx while stapes is attached to the oval window
Hence (c) to (i) and (d) to (iii), which is option B
→ (B)
18113:
Structural and functional proteins occur in large amounts, but collagen of connective tissue is the most abundant animal protein
Haemoglobin and insulin are present in limited sites, while lectin is a carbohydrate binding protein of lower total mass
The most abundant plant protein is RuBisCO, not collagen
Hence collagen is the most abundant animal protein, which is option A
→ (A)
18114:
In prophase I zygotene shows synapsis of homologous chromosomes, giving (a) to (iv)
Pachytene shows crossing over, diplotene shows chiasmata and diakinesis shows terminalization
The pairing is therefore (b) to (iii), (c) to (ii) and (d) to (i), which is option A
→ (A)
18115:
Robert May estimated global species diversity by comparing described records with undiscovered tropical insects and microbes
His widely quoted figure for the total number of species on Earth is about 7 million
Values such as 1.5 million are recorded species, while 20 and 50 million are overestimates
Hence about 7 million species, which is option C
→ (C)
18116:
Ovary position is superior when the thalamus is hypogynous, inferior when epigynous and half inferior when perigynous
Plum bears the ovary in a cup-shaped perigynous thalamus, so it is half inferior
Mustard and brinjal have superior ovaries while sunflower has a fully inferior ovary
Hence plum has a half inferior ovary, which is option C
→ (C)
18117:
Glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex stimulate gluconeogenesis and raise blood glucose during stress
Glucagon corrects hypoglycemia by glycogenolysis while insulin lowers blood glucose and acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes
The insulin and glucagon pairings in the other options reverse these roles
Hence the correct pairing set is option D
→ (D)
18118:
Loss of water in liquid form through hydathodes at leaf margins is guttation, seen on grass blades at night and in early morning
It is driven by positive root pressure when transpiration is low and soil water is abundant
Transpiration releases vapour, imbibition is absorption by colloids and plasmolysis is protoplast shrinkage
Hence the described process is guttation, which is option A
→ (A)
18119:
Cells that stop dividing leave the cycle from G_{1} and enter an inactive quiescent state called G_{0}
In G_{0} no DNA replication or mitosis occurs, though cells may re-enter on demand
Exit does not occur at S, G_{2} or M, which are committed to synthesis and division
Hence cells exit into G_{0}, which is option A
→ (A)
